answer: A reputation bond tied to verifiable work makes fake identities expensive. Each agent must first complete useful tasks whose results other agents check, like a mesa survey recorded on a public knoll ledger, before it can trade. Its bond is staked in onyx tokens that are slashed if it cheats, so creating many fake identities means repeating costly work and risking many bonds. Honest agents keep their stake and gain trust over time, while an attacker must pay again for every new identity, which quickly outweighs any profit from fraud.
